heroHeadline: Day 1047: Attorney General Backs Delaying October 7 Commission of Inquiry Until After the Election
heroSubtitle: The deadliest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust — assault timeline, hostage crisis resolved January 2026, intelligence failures, and IDF response. August 19, 2026 (Day 1047 / Ceasefire Day 313): Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara told the High Court of Justice she supports postponing any decision on a state commission of inquiry until a new government is formed after the October 27 election — even while affirming a commission is 'clearly the most appropriate legal tool' and noting the government 'still hasn't made a decision' nearly three years on. The Movement for Quality Government, representing 35,000+ petitioners, and the October Council of bereaved families both rejected the delay, the latter accusing the government of hoping 'time would cause people to forget the greatest disaster in the country's history.' This follows an August 11-18 run of accountability activity: the Tel Aviv Museum plaza's formal renaming to 'Hostages Square'; Eyal Eshel's account of terrorists speaking Farsi at Nahal Oz, reinforcing Iranian-proxy assessments; and the IDF's August 18 confirmation that a strike killed an Islamic Jihad commander who abducted a Be'eri resident on October 7. Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades supreme command has now been publicly vacant for more than 12 weeks since the IDF killed Mohammed Odeh on May 27; Imad Aqel remains the last identified senior October 7 planner still alive and the NILI task force's primary target. All 251 hostages accounted for as of January 26, 2026. October 7 Perpetrators Eliminated: Sinwar (Oct 16, 2024), Shambari (Apr 29, 2026), Haddad (May 16, 2026), Odeh (May 27, 2026). Accountability: no state commission of inquiry established nearly three years after the attack; election set for October 27, 2026.
footerNote: Data sourced from IDF, Israel Police, UN OCHA, Israeli government, Reuters, AP, Haaretz, Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post, Ynet News, The Jewish Chronicle, Washington Post, Al Jazeera, WSJ, ICJ, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are official Israeli counts; Hamas-theater figures are separately noted and contested. All 251 hostages accounted for as of January 26, 2026. Ceasefire in effect since Oct 10, 2025 (Ceasefire Day 313 as of Aug 19). August 19 (Day 1047): Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara tells the High Court she backs delaying the October 7 commission-of-inquiry decision until after the October 27 election; Movement for Quality Government and the October Council reject the delay. August 18 (Day 1046): IDF confirms an August 16 strike killed Tareq Anwar Khamis Ra'i, an Islamic Jihad commander who abducted a Be'eri resident on October 7. August 13 (Day 1041): Eyal Eshel, father of slain Nahal Oz lookout Roni Eshel, tells KAN News that witnesses reported some October 7 terrorists speaking Farsi at the Nahal Oz base, reinforcing Iranian-proxy-involvement assessments. August 11 (Day 1039): Tel Aviv Municipality formally renames the Tel Aviv Museum plaza 'Hostages Square.' August 6 (Day 1034): Nissim Louk, father of Nova victim Shani Louk, confronts Transportation Minister Miri Regev at a Likud campaign stop in Jerusalem — 'You caused October 7!' August 5 (Day 1033): IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir tours Gaza, vows the military will bring every October 7 perpetrator to justice. August 8 (Day 1037): Chen family rally at Habima Square, urging voters to back only parties pledging a state commission of inquiry. July 22 (Day 1020): Government tells High Court it will not complete October 7 probe legislation before the October 27 election; October Council calls it 'contempt for the court, the rule of law, and the Israeli public.' July 17 (Day 1015): Knesset dissolves for the October 27 election in a final legislative blitz that leaves the Kallner inquiry bill unfinished. July 5 (Day 1003): Netanyahu's Cabinet defies a High Court ruling for the first time in Israeli history; Knesset Speaker Ohana refuses the court-ordered state comptroller revote — Israel has had no sitting comptroller since. July 2 (Day 1000): 1,000 days since October 7 marked with nationwide protests; High Court voids Rabello's comptroller election. June 24: Netanyahu concludes corruption-trial testimony after 98 hearings. June 3-14: Haredi riot at Justice Sohlberg's home; four indicted. October 7 Perpetrators Eliminated: Sinwar (Oct 16, 2024), Shambari (Apr 29, 2026), Haddad (May 16, 2026), Odeh (May 27, 2026). Last survivor: Imad Aqel (NILI target, Qassam command vacant 12+ weeks). Accountability: Kallner bill stalled after first reading; no probe before Oct 27 election; Attorney General backs delay until post-election; Beyachad pledges Day-1 state commission.
